My car loan company told me specifically that they cannot charge me interest on any money I have already sent them, even if the money is applied to future payments instead of being applied directly to principal, so I assumed that the time share would work the same way.

Details that might matter:

  • I live in MD

  • The timeshare interest is compounded daily.

It all depends on what you signed. Almost anything can be legal. And a interest compounded 365 days... sounds brutal.
It's really not that much worse than it compounding e.g. weekly.
you started off with "timeshare", so your probably getting legally fucked over somehow.

Not sure if the car loan guy told you the truth or there was miscommunication, but I personally have never seen a loan where future payments reduce the cost of the interest.

You either get one of two benefits but not both: Not worry about payments for a couple months or having your interest reduced and your loan paid off quicker.

For example,

I have 50, $100 payments.

I pay $1000 one month and apply that to principal. You will make less total payments because you already paid some and interest will be saved.

I pay $1000 one month and apply that to future payments. Now I don't have to pay my loan for 9 more months, but it will basically just be like I still paid those 9 payments on the normal schedule they are just doing it automatically now.

I think OP meant that he was trying to make a payment on the principal, and was told that he could only make payments 'in advance'. I'm guessing there are terms in the contract that say he cannot make payments on the principal. That's a pretty shit contract condition because now he has to pay the maximum amount of interest over the life of the loan.

Yes. You should have put that extra money down as the down payment, and your total loan and interest would be lower. They are under no obligation to reward you immediately for early repayment unless it says so in that loan document.
